assessment_summary: In step 0025, the author claims that 'every subgroup of S_7 generated by two 7-cycles is either a cyclic group of order 7, the group PSL(2,7) we want, or all of S_7'. This is factually false. A 7-cycle is an even permutation (it can be written as 6 transpositions), so any group generated by 7-cycles must be a subgroup of the alternating group A_7. It is mathematically impossible for two 7-cycles to generate the full symmetric group S_7 (which contains odd permutations). The correct list of possible groups is C_7, PSL(2,7), or A_7. Although A_7 would also be ruled out by the same 'too many automorphisms' logic, the mathematical theorem stated as justification is false, making the step invalid.
